records.title: Add SM120 split-KV (FlashDecoding) with FP32 partial outputs
records.body:
## Summary

- Add split-KV (FlashDecoding) support for SM120 (Blackwell GeForce / DGX Spark) — enables `num_splits > 1` for decode-like workloads with short Q and long K
- FP32 partial outputs: split-KV kernel writes FP32 accumulators directly to GMEM, bypassing SMEM to preserve full precision for the combine kernel
- Paged KV support removed from this PR per review feedback — will be a separate follow-up

Builds on #2329, #2330, #2333.

## Key changes

**flash_fwd.py (FlashAttentionForwardBase + FlashAttentionForwardSm80)**:
- `is_split_kv` parameter wired through `__init__`, `_check_type` (allow FP32 mO), epilogue (`split_idx` O/LSE indexing), `__call__` (O/LSE layout transposes with split dimension, num_splits through tile scheduler), and kernel body
- Kernel body wrapped in `n_block_max > n_block_min` guard for empty-split correctness
- Remaining-iterations loop uses `n_block - n_block_min` to stop at split boundary
- **FP32 direct write epilogue**: for `o_dtype != dtype`, bypasses SMEM entirely and writes MMA accumulators directly to GMEM via `thr_mma.partition_C(gO)` with per-element bounds checking. This avoids the SMEM store/load layout mismatch between `make_tiled_copy_C` (MMA accumulator layout) and `gmem_tiled_copy_O` (GMEM coalescing layout) that corrupts FP32 data through SMEM.

**interface.py**:
- `out_partial` allocated as FP32 `torch.zeros`, `lse_partial` as `torch.full(-inf)`
- `is_split_kv` passed to SM120 constructor

**flash_fwd_sm120.py**:
- `can_implement` unchanged (FP32 direct write doesn't use SMEM for output)

## Validation on SM121a (DGX Spark)

```
Split-KV: 14/14 configs pass
  - num_splits: 2, 4
  - causal and non-causal
  - Sq=16/32/64/128/256, Sk=256/512/1024
  - H=1/2/4/8, D=64/128
  - split_diff matches nosplit precision (0.001-0.002 vs reference)

Non-split regression: 5/5 configs pass
  - B=1/2, Sq=64/128/256, Sk=64/128/256
  - causal and non-causal, D=64/128
```

Contributed by Second Nature Computing (https://joinsecondnature.com)

records.title: [Fwd,Sm100] TMA-paged KV cache loading for small page sizes
records.body:
## Summary

Experimental TMA-paged KV cache loading for SM100/SM110. Uses hardware TMA (`cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d`) instead of software `cp.async` for paged KV when `page_size < tile_n`.

**Gate conditions** (auto-detected, no user API change):
- SM100/SM110 only
- `pages_per_nblock ∈ {2, 4, 8}` (page_size divides tile_n with power-of-2 ratio)
- `head_dim * elem_size ≤ 128` (single TMA tile per page — currently head_dim=64 for bf16)

Adds 1 constructor param (`paged_kv_page_size`) to `FlashAttentionForwardSm100`. Everything else is derived internally.

## Performance (GB200 SM100a, GQA nhq=32 nhkv=8, bf16, head_dim=64)

### Prefill — 6-8% gain at seqlen ≥ 4K

| seqlen | ps | cp.async (ms) | TMA-paged (ms) | delta |
|--------|----|---------------|----------------|-------|
| 4096   | 32 | 0.193         | 0.181          | **-6.2%** |
| 4096   | 64 | 0.193         | 0.177          | **-8.3%** |
| 8192   | 32 | 0.617         | 0.565          | **-8.4%** |
| 8192   | 64 | 0.643         | 0.591          | **-8.1%** |
| 1024   | 32 | 0.082         | 0.082          | 0%    |

### Decode — neutral (bandwidth-bound, ~0.085ms)

No meaningful difference. Decode kernels are too short for TMA overhead to matter.

## Why head_dim=64 only

TMA hardware limits `boxDim[0] * elem_size ≤ 128` bytes with 128B swizzle. For bf16 this means `head_dim ≤ 64` for a single TMA tile per page. head_dim=128 would require atom-level TMAs (8 rows × 64 elements each, 32 ops per load_KV) which adds complexity for marginal gain:

- **hd=128 decode**: slightly worse (32 small TMAs from one thread > all-thread cp.async)
- **hd=128 prefill 4K**: only 2-3% gain
- **hd=128 SMEM layout**: K-major and MN-major atoms tile differently, requiring empirically-derived offset formulas — fragile

## Conclusion

This PR demonstrates the approach and benchmarks. **Recommend abandoning** — the 6-8% prefill gain for head_dim=64 does not justify the code complexity (host CUDA driver calls, TMA descriptor caching, raw PTX copies). A cleaner future approach would use `cute.copy(tma_atom, ...)` per page with SMEM tensor slicing, leveraging CuTe's layout algebra instead of manual offset math.

records.title: fix(hd256/sm100): make the dedicated hd256 kernel stride-aware (supersede #2666 copy)
records.body: Fixes #2665. Supersedes the `.contiguous()` stop-gap from #2666. ## Summary The dedicated head_dim=256 SM100 (Blackwell) forward kernel built its q/k/v CuTe layouts with strides synthesized from shape assuming a fully-contiguous BSHD tensor) and reused only the input's base pointer. maybe_contiguous() in the interface only guarantees stride(-1) == 1, so a transpose(1, 2) -ed input — contiguous in the head dim but with swapped sequence/head strides — reached the kernel and produced TMA loads from the wrong addresses, silently corrupting outputs on B200 at `head_dim=256` (#2665). Other head dims and H100 were unaffected because they use kernels that already honor arbitrary input strides. #2666 worked around this by forcing q/k/v contiguous before the kernel, which adds a full copy (~0.4 GB for the issue's `1×32×8192×256` shape) on every forward in the common transposed-input case. **This PR makes the kernel honor the real input strides instead, so the copy is no longer needed.** ## Root cause python # before: strides synthesized from shape, base pointer reused q_layout = cute.make_layout( (s_q_total, d, ((h_r, h_k), b)), stride=(d64 * h_r64 * h_k64, 1, ((d64, d64 * h_r64), stride_b_qo)), # assumes contiguous ) q = cute.make_tensor(q_tensor.iterator, q_layout) This is consistent with how the **general** SM100 forward kernel (`flash_fwd_sm100.py`) and the **hd256 backward** kernels already work — both derive their layouts from the actual tensor strides. The hd256 forward was the only kernel still assuming contiguity. ## Changes - Forward (dense + paged): derive the sequence / head / batch strides from the actual q/k/v tensors for the rank-5, rank-4, and rank-3 (varlen) paths. The `d` (head_dim) mode is kept a **static `1`** — TMA requires the contiguous innermost mode's stride to be statically known, and `maybe_contiguous()` guarantees `stride(-1) == 1`. - Backward: the hd256 backward kernels already derive layouts from real strides, so #2666's backward .contiguous()` was redundant and is removed. - interface.py`: replace the unconditional copy with an **alignment-gated guard** (`maybe_hd256_compatible_contiguous`) that copies only when an input stride would violate the kernel's 16-byte / divby-64 TMA assumptions. This keeps the zero-copy fast path for the common case while staying safe for exotic (e.g. sliced/padded) strides. ## Validation (B200) | Check | Result | |--------|--------| | #2665 repro (transposed, `1×32×8192×256`) | max_abs_err `0.155` → **`4.9e-4`** | | Forward, transposed vs contiguous (same kernel), MHA/GQA/causal | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Backward, transposed vs contiguous — `out`/`dq`/`dk`/`dv`, MHA/GQA/causal | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Paged-KV, non-contiguous q (same kernel) | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Padded-stride fallback (e.g. stride `(…, 257, 1)`) | guard fires, result correct | For a contiguous input the derived strides are arithmetically identical to the old synthesized ones, so the existing supported path is bit-identical to before. ## Test plan - pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` on the `d=256` slice (forward + backward): **240 passed, 648 skipped** (skips = feature combos hd256 doesn't support: softcap / learnable_sink / local). - ruff check flash_attn/cute/` — clean. - tests ran are summarized in the table below: - ## Notes Developed as two independent implementations that converged on the same design (including the non-obvious TMA static-`1` requirement) and cross-validated each other's results on separate B200s. ## Coauthor: Coauthor: @oattia

records.title: [FA2] Fix backward for non-contiguous Q/K/V inputs
records.body:
## Summary

- allocate FA2 backward output buffers with a contiguous last dimension when the saved Q/K/V layout requires it
- preserve the existing outer layout for inputs whose last dimension is already contiguous
- cover dense and varlen attention with both separate Q/K/V and KV-packed public APIs

## Problem

FA2 forward accepts Q/K/V tensors whose last dimension has stride greater than one because the CUDA wrapper normalizes them before launch. The high-level autograd Functions save the original inputs, however, and backward currently uses torch.empty_like for dQ/dK/dV.

For a non-overlapping-dense transposed input, empty_like preserves that input layout. The resulting gradient buffer is then passed as a mutable output to the C++ backward API, which requires stride(-1) == 1 and fails, for example:

    RuntimeError: dq must have contiguous last dimension

This affects dense and varlen separate-QKV APIs, plus dQ in both KV-packed APIs. The QKV-packed dQKV and KV-packed dKV buffers are already created from explicit contiguous shapes and remain unchanged.

The regression became visible after the custom-op refactor in #1139 stopped returning normalized Q/K/V tensors to the outer autograd context.

## Fix

A shared allocation helper centralizes the CUDA mutable-output invariant:

- if stride(-1) is already 1, use preserve_format exactly as empty_like did before
- otherwise, allocate contiguous_format so the CUDA backward ABI can write the result

This changes allocation layout only for inputs that previously failed; it adds no copy to supported inputs.

## Tests

RTX 5090:

- 4 new cases passed: dense/varlen x separate-QKV/KV-packed
- outputs and all input gradients are bitwise equal to contiguous-input references under deterministic backward
- 32 existing non-contiguous-dout backward cases passed
- eager and torch.compile non-contiguous forward/backward checks passed
- helper policy check confirms valid outer strides are preserved and invalid last-dimension layouts become contiguous
- combined post-rebase run: 36 passed
- git diff --check passed

records.title: [CuTe] Add packed QKV and KV public APIs
records.body:
## Summary

Add the four packed-input public facades that users of the FA2 API expect:

- `flash_attn_qkvpacked_func`
- `flash_attn_kvpacked_func`
- `flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked_func`
- `flash_attn_varlen_kvpacked_func`

They are exported from `flash_attn.cute` and documented alongside the existing unpacked APIs.

## Motivation

CuTe currently exports only `flash_attn_func` and `flash_attn_varlen_func`. Models whose projection already produces packed QKV or KV tensors must manually split those tensors and lose API parity when moving from FA2 to the CuTe/FA4 path.

The new entry points accept the established packed layouts, including GQA/MQA KV with fewer heads, and preserve one packed input gradient through autograd.

## Implementation

A small shared validator checks the packed axis and returns `unbind` views. Each public facade then delegates to the existing dense or varlen CuTe API with the complete CuTe option set.

No attention kernel, scheduler, or backward implementation is duplicated. Autograd joins the view gradients into a contiguous gradient matching the packed input.

The explicit thin functions are intentional public API and cross-family compatibility boundaries; keeping full signatures makes them discoverable and inspectable.

## Validation

RTX 5090 focused suite: 17 passed.

Coverage includes:

- dense and varlen QKV-packed MHA;
- dense and varlen KV-packed GQA;
- causal and non-causal forward/backward numerical equality with unpacked CuTe calls;
- contiguous packed gradients;
- all four APIs under `torch.compile`;
- all four APIs in FakeTensor forward/backward;
- focused invalid-rank and invalid-packed-axis errors.

Ruff, `py_compile`, and whitespace checks pass. On unmodified main, the same test module fails collection because the four public symbols do not exist.

## Compatibility and scope

These are CuTe-native facades: they keep the CuTe option set and `(out, lse)` return contract rather than emulating FA2 dropout or attention-probability returns. Paged KV is forwarded only on architectures where the underlying CuTe implementation supports it. No claim is made that the wrapper itself improves kernel latency.

records.title: [CuTe, SM100] writeback LSE to shared memory when `return_lse=False` to avoid compiler-induced 14% perf diff
records.body:
Addresses https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/2729

@drisspg observed toggling the `return_lse` flag to True to write back log-sum-exp to gmem resulted in 19% speedup on B200 at size `(B, S, H, D) = (2, 16384, 16, 64)`. I was able to repro the performance gap (14% though, not 19%) for these sizes using his script. this table is from running off main on a single B200.

| Shape | return_lse=False | return_lse=True | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B2 S2048 H16 D64 | 0.0613 ms | 0.0492 ms | 1.245× |
| B2 S8192 H16 D64 | 0.7624 ms | 0.6420 ms | 1.188× |
| B2 S16384 H16 D64 | 3.0153 ms | 2.6366 ms | 1.144× |

This PR updates the output correction loop so even if `mLSE` is none we will still construct the log-sum-exp per-query and at least writeback to the shared memory state storing row-sum and row-max and this seems to resolve the compiler cliff.

Benchmarks on the above sizes from my branch on a B200.

| Shape | return_lse=False | return_lse=True | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B2 S2048 H16 D64 | 0.0492 ms | 0.0492 ms | 1.000× |
| B2 S8192 H16 D64 | 0.6211 ms | 0.6353 ms | 0.978× |
| B2 S16384 H16 D64 | 2.5670 ms | 2.5687 ms | 0.999× |

and the perf gap seems to be closed with this change.


For the `return_lse=True` path this should have no behavior change and we can confirm this by seeing the compiled ptx is byte identical for `B2 S16384 H16 D64` and `return_lse=True` by setting the `CUTE_DSL_KEEP_PTX` environment variable and inspecting the dumped ptx and compare the dumped ptx from this branch and from main.

records.title: [None][feat] add Rubin topology and prototype locality-domain sharding to GVR V2 decode
records.body:
## Dependency

Built on #18446. Keep this PR in Draft and rebase after #18446 lands. Companion prefill work is in #18764.

## Summary

- Extend GVR V2 self-sampling decode to SM107 using runtime SM topology instead of B200-specific constants.
- Add a default-off `use_gvr_locality_domain` prototype that splits eligible decode requests across two Rubin locality domains.
- Keep each request and its `next_n` rows together, with proportional partitioning based on the reported domain SM counts.
- Preserve the existing full-device path for BS=1, small workloads, unsupported configurations, and whenever the prototype is disabled.
- Fail closed on cold CUDA Graph capture, device/topology mismatch, silent partition-context failure, or invalid unsplit tensor geometry.

## Current scope

This is topology enablement plus an experimental GVR-only compute-sharding path, not a completed maximum-performance Rubin implementation.

- The indexer logits producer still runs on the full device.
- The produced logits remain ordinary global allocations; they are not domain-local.
- TMA, PDL, domain-local logits/K-cache allocation, producer-side locality, and BS=1 column sharding/merge are not implemented here.
- Dispatch thresholds are provisional and must be derived from R200 measurements before any default-on or whitelist decision.
- The prototype supports one in-flight model execution per CUDA device. Concurrent GraphExec replay or multiple engines sharing a device are not supported yet because the execution-domain workspaces/events are shared.
- Each eligible graph shape must run eagerly once through the same `TopK` instance before capture.
- The new public prototype field requires the normal telemetry/privacy CODEOWNER review.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- GVR host router tests: 11/11.
- Locality planner/orchestration tests: 17/17 through a dependency-stub harness.
- Planner property sweeps over BS=1-1024, compressed N=4K-256K, K={512,1024,2048}, supported `next_n`, and symmetric/asymmetric topologies; all eligible plans were request-aligned, disjoint, and exhaustive.
- Existing B200 route parity: 21,504 route cases and 43,008 streaming comparisons.
- Relevant pre-commit formatting/lint, Python compilation, DCO, and whitespace checks.

R200 kernel validation has not been completed. Full package/DSA pytest collection is blocked in the current environment by an external `bindings.so` mismatch (`global_steady_clock_now`), and the installed CuTe DSL does not provide the Rubin helper needed to compile the SM107 path. The stub tests are not a substitute for SM107 execution.

## Draft exit criteria

Before marking Ready, run correctness, stability, and performance A/B on R200 for:

- Every integer BS from 1 through 1024 for route/correctness coverage, with performance focus around domain-SM and routing boundaries.
- Compressed N={4K,8K,16K,32K,64K,128K,256K} (V4 ISL/4).
- K={512,1024,2048}, compression ratios {1,4}, and supported `next_n` values.
- Full-device versus strict/balanced locality-domain execution.
- Eager execution, warmup/capture, and at least 1,000 alternating CUDA Graph replays.
- GVR-only latency and indexer-producer + GVR end-to-end latency with CUDA Graph/PDL settings recorded.
- Random and real indexer logits, variable/short rows, ties, denormals, and `+/-inf`; keep the existing NaN contract separate.

The results must justify or retune the provisional dispatch gate and confirm that SM100/SM103 code generation and all fallbacks remain unchanged.

records.title: [None][feat] Add PrimsTS MoE with Rubin locality domains
records.body:
## Description

Add `moe_config.backend: PRIMS_TS` for NVFP4/BF16 MoE on Blackwell and Rubin, and MXFP4/MXFP8 MoE on Blackwell. Kimi K3 NVFP4 SiTU uses the vendored PrimsTS grouped GEMMs with existing TRT-LLM weight layouts, routing and external expert communication.

Sources from [FlashInfer PR #4361](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4361) are pinned to `bc00583287cad89af09d10a9880c538fa037ebd8`. Vendoring follows [attention PR #17399](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17399): source lock, downstream patch, integrity checks and package data. Most added lines are vendored code.

```yaml
moe_config:
  backend: PRIMS_TS
```

The backend preserves FP32 K3 router logits/corrections, hybrid fused routing, PDL readiness dependencies and stable CUDA Graph workspace shapes. Implementation registration probes DSL dependencies lazily; the LLM args manifest includes the compatible backend option.

Optional Rubin locality uses the existing policy, runtime and localized allocation pools. Each domain owns output-channel shards of both GEMMs and their scales. FC1 writes a shared full-width intermediate, both FC1 partitions join before FC2, and both partitions share one compiled GEMM per FC. Output/scales pointers retain full leading strides. Localized autotuning measures concurrent partitions and includes the actual compute topology in its identity.

The locality execution path now:
- Preserves K3 hybrid routing and `TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL` instead of adding explicit one-token top-k/cast work and disabling PDL.
- Fuses FC2 weighted finalization into BF16 bulk reduction into a zeroed final output, avoiding expanded FC2 storage and standalone unpermutation.
- Tunes FC1 TMA activation multicast across two/four independent output tiles with one/two-CTA MMA groups.
- Uses a merged A/B TMA barrier and, for eligible NVFP4 paths, one producer for weights and weight scales; MMA copies weight scales to TMEM while a separate task converts activation scales.
- Uses static persistent work scheduling for multicast variants, with resident-cluster budgets scaled to actual locality SM counts. Existing LDGSTS/CLC alternatives remain eligible.
- Keeps all activation TMA loading warps in multicast senders and only the barrier-signaling warp per MMA group in receivers, while preserving register redistribution for every assigned warp.

Compact routed TMA descriptors use the actual token count. Non-routed stacked activations declare a single expert-coordinate extent; weights retain their expert axis. Local PDL task resources use CuTe wrappers with explicit compiler memory ordering. Fused weight-scale TMEM layout is checked during CPU schedule construction and device compilation. Fused finalize rounds each weighted contribution to BF16 and accumulates in an unordered BF16 reduction; its arithmetic differs from the standalone FP32 reduction.

SM100/SM103/SM107 are gated explicitly. BF16 supports SwiGLU, NVFP4 supports SwiGLU/SiTU, and MXFP4/MXFP8 is Blackwell-only. SM107 uses K=128 OMMA and requires CUTLASS DSL Rubin helpers; incorrect N=256 token-tile variants are excluded. Locality requires H divisible by 256 and per-rank I by 128. Unsupported expert bias, MoE LoRA, EPLB, DWDP and fused shared experts are rejected.

The PR also repairs mixed-batch KDA fallback core shape and releases stale primary-allocator cache before enabled MoE migration, allowing full K3 weight localization. Existing backend defaults remain unchanged; PrimsTS and locality are opt-in.

## Validation

Earlier execution validation at `281ce2ad1f`:
- B200: **101 tests passed, 46 architecture skips** across the PrimsTS and locality test files.
- Actual K3 MoE geometry H3584/I3072, 112 local of 896 experts, top-16 SiTU, N=1/16/1024: eager comparisons and 20 changed-FP32-routing CUDA Graph replays per shape pass with PDL enabled.
- Twelve BF16/NVFP4 regressions at N16/N1024 force one resident cluster, exercising repeated expert work tiles, fused/unfused finalization and changed routing indices/weights in graphs.
- Unfused partitioned outputs are bitwise equal to ordinary PrimsTS. Fused-finalize relative L2 is approximately 0.34–0.36% in the K3 geometry checks, within the 2% same-quantized-operator comparison gate.
- CPU construction passes for 112 resident multicast schedule variants. Vendor patch/lock integrity, pre-commit and DCO checks pass.
- Compute Sanitizer 2026.3 with explicit `--check-tensor-ops yes`: the three K3 stress shapes and full 101-test suite pass, exit0 and zero errors.

Explicit TMA checking found an invalid FC2 activation descriptor extent at N1. The corrected descriptor passes the full tensor-op instrumented suite. Before the receiver repair, default-option instrumentation (tensor-op checking disabled) stalled at N1024 first graph replay after eager fused/unfused comparisons passed. The local PDL ordering change alone did not eliminate it. The committed receiver repair now passes both sanitizer modes on Rubin, as recorded below.

**Rubin validation before the receiver repair:** commit `281ce2ad1f` passes **167 tests with 44 architecture skips**, exit0, on an actual ARM/SM107 node. Coverage includes BF16/NVFP4, localized allocations/compute streams, fused routing/finalization and changing-input CUDA Graphs. Both allocated four-GPU nodes validate all 3747 source/native file hashes and identical package versions.

The current 8192-token native MLA probe reproduces the earlier FMHA CGA legality error. Both nodes pass its context/two-decode-step reference with the same experiment-only GMEM override and matching NVRTC 13.4.59. This setup condition applies to every upcoming full-model arm and is outside this PR.

**Multicast receiver repair (`c4b7715903`):** long graph replay exposed an N256/tactic `(32,137,4)` stall in both localized and ordinary full-GPU execution, including a control that never creates locality contexts. GPU core dumps identify non-leading activation-loading warps in a receiver CTA waiting on an empty-barrier phase. Those warps issue neither TMA data nor barrier arrivals, so participating warps can lap them around the ring. Receiver tasks now retain only their signaling warp; all assigned warps still participate in register redistribution.

The matching final task prototype passes the existing **167 Rubin tests plus two new deep-pipeline replay regressions**. Four long-replay controls with the final register handling each complete **2.88 million MoE calls**, followed by changed-route numerical gates: full-GPU R4, localized R4 with two FC2 tactics/PDL settings, and localized R2. Two earlier prototype controls also complete. Deliberately delaying idle receiver warps stalls the original first call; the corrected participation passes the same delayed eager/graph protocol. Both Rubin nodes now verify the committed source and native files. The exact committed source passes **169 tests with 44 architecture skips**, exit0, including the two new deep-pipeline regressions. The expanded operator sweep is running; these checks establish execution correctness for the tested cases, not full-model accuracy or performance.

On Rubin, the committed source passes **both default-option memcheck and explicit `--check-tensor-ops yes`**, each with exit0, zero sanitizer errors and 20 changing-route graphs at K3 N1024, tactic `(8,18,4)`, PDL enabled. These single-rank checks select CPU-only MPI components; distributed model runs do not use that MPI diagnostic condition. The previously reproduced default-option stall is resolved in this Rubin check.

**Outstanding for this draft:** complete the full tactic sweep after the receiver repair, then latest Rubin operator/full-model performance and accuracy measurements. No current full-model accuracy or performance-parity claim is made.

Earlier revisions passed clean native builds for `100-real;103-real` and separately `107-real`, independent BF16/FP32 and NVFP4 SiTU references, Rubin locality/allocator regressions and mixed-batch KDA regressions. Those results do not replace validation of the new fused arithmetic and execution schedule on Rubin.

## B200 execution ablations before the receiver repair

All six cases pass eager/graph numerical gates on commit `281ce2ad1f`. The complete run retains 1,200 measurements. These are **fixed-base-config execution comparisons on ordinary streams**, with 50 alternating forward/reverse timing rounds and 16 calls per graph. They are neither separately autotuned backend comparisons nor measurements of Rubin hardware locality. Inputs use H3584/I3072, local112/global896, top16 and FP32 routing; input quantization is excluded.

| Dtype / tokens | Full R1, unfused (us) | Full R4, fused (us) | Two ordinary streams, R4 fused (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 / 1 | 25.054 | 20.844 | 27.600 |
| NVFP4 / 16 | 145.332 | 123.504 | 122.757 |
| NVFP4 / 1024 | 1379.209 | 829.298 | 830.795 |
| BF16 / 1 | 49.369 | 54.062 | 58.205 |
| BF16 / 16 | 242.556 | 257.833 | 270.876 |
| BF16 / 1024 | 600.196 | 599.287 | 601.303 |

Base tactics are `(8,18)` for NVFP4 SiTU and `(64,0)` for BF16 SwiGLU. R4 includes resident multicast, merged A/B stages and eligible mixed weight-scale loading. The NVFP4 improvements and BF16 small-batch regressions support keeping the existing candidates and tuning on the actual device; R4 is not forced. At one token, ordinary partition streams add overhead without Rubin's local allocation/compute domains. Raw samples and the full-finalize-only control are retained in the execution audit.

## Earlier complete-model measurements

These measurements predate the current execution changes and are retained as baselines.

On eight VR200 GPUs, the previous MoE-only locality implementation produced:

| Concurrency | Off output tok/s | On output tok/s | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 45.729 | 42.758 | -6.50% |
| 8 | 185.968 | 184.547 | -0.76% |
| 16 | 278.648 | 276.944 | -0.61% |

TP8/EP8, ISL8192/OSL1024, seed 37, no drafter, OFF/ON/ON/OFF ordering; all 900 formal requests completed. Approximately 2.3% OFF baseline drift exceeds the C8/C16 aggregate effects. Both arms used the same experiment-only FMHA GMEM-reduction override because unmodified native FMHA failed its long-KV CGA legality check in that setup. The override is outside this PR. Other shared controls included PyTorch 26.05, CUDA 13.4.59, experimental Triton SM107 support and NCCL collectives without NVLS multicast.

At decode batch 1, earlier profiles showed the MoE envelope rising from 20.327 to 35.289 us/layer, including about 11 us of extra routing-kernel work. The new routing/PDL path addresses that measured integration overhead, but its resulting Rubin complete-model latency is not yet measured.

Earlier full GSM8K (1319 documents/arm, five-shot, seed 0, no drafter, max output 256) gave locality OFF **96.1334%** and ON **96.6641%**, passing the disclosed adapted **93.2975%** gate. The repository reference has no exact NVFP4/no-drafter entry. These scores predate fused finalization and do not establish current model accuracy.

Separately, ordinary PrimsTS on eight B300 GPUs achieved **80.5265 versus 80.7283 output tok/s** against TRTLLM-Gen at C1 (-0.25%), after the FC2 PDL fix. Full GSM8K gave PrimsTS 97.0432% strict / 97.1190% flexible versus TRTLLM-Gen 96.4367%. These are Blackwell results from before the locality changes.

Reproduction commands, complete outputs, source/runtime manifests and profiles are retained under `/home/scratch.qgai_sw/qgai/project/qgai/primsTSforMOE_artifacts/`; the current execution audit is in `ugpu_alignment_20260913/report.md`, and prior complete-model results are in `ugpu_fullmodel_20260913/report.md`.

- [x] Implementation documentation and relevant tests included.

- [x] Vendored provenance/downstream patch and LLM args manifest updated.

records.title: [None][perf] Fuse strided MXFP8 packing for cuDNN attention
records.body:
Automatically pack eligible BF16 Q/K/V tensors directly into cuDNN's MXFP8 payload and scale layouts. The CuTe kernels remove intermediate layout copies while preserving the native quantization arithmetic. Dispatch selects the fast path on SM100 for supported shapes and strides; unsupported inputs keep the native implementation. No configuration flag is required.

The full-model comparison uses Wan2.2 A14B with the official static-NVFP4 checkpoint on one B200: 480×832, 33 frames, 40 steps, seed 42, three prompts, CUDNN MXFP8 attention, compilation on and CUDA graphs off. Both arms use TensorRT-LLM `1.3.0rc27.dev202609150000` in the same process.

| Full-generation latency | Native | Candidate | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean of prompt medians | 21.57 s | 20.05 s | 7.06% |

Validation: byte-level payload/scale and cuDNN consumer checks passed; production GPU tests: **34 passed and one expected SM103 hardware skip**. Worst-prompt LPIPS across all 33 frames: **0.0** (limit 0.25).

records.title: [None][perf] MXFP8 locality-domain split: one parent reset for both shards, static planner decision
records.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #19469 (merged as f94eeb3738). Three commits:

1. **One parent reset for both locality-domain shards** (below).
2. **Static planner decision, shards as the only weight copy** (see below).
3. **[chore] Drop the cached-FC2 tactic from the split** so its tactic space equals the full-GPU op's and cannot be misled by warm profiling (concurrent partition tuning cannot use the cold-L2 mode). No measurable performance change (table at the end).

 The MXFP8 locality-domain split of the fused FC12 MoE launched each shard through the full fused op, so a split call paid two workspace resets, a standalone output memset (with its aux-stream event pair) and, because raw activations could not be handed to two concurrent shards, a standalone `mxfp8_quantize` launch. Those launches cost more than the split's kernel-level locality gain, which is why `enable_locality_domains` was neutral to slightly negative per MoE call.

This PR runs **one parent reset for both shards** on the caller's stream before the fork:

- `fused_fc12_workspace.py`: the reset kernel takes an optional second workspace (ready flags + two counters) and clears both partitions in one launch.
- `cute_dsl_custom_ops.py`: `Sm107Mxfp8FusedFc12MoeRunner` gains `skip_reset` (shard launches do no reset and require E4M3 input), class-level accessors for the cached sync workspace and input-quant scratch, and `launch_locality_domain_parent_reset` (both workspaces, whole-output clear under `zero_output`, BF16/FP16 -> MXFP8 quantization into the shared scratch, PDL against the preceding kernel). The composite op `cute_dsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12_moe_locality_domain_inplace_rubin` gains `zero_output`, registers the parent reset as the concurrent tuning runner's prologue and launches the skip-reset runner directly per partition (no nested custom op).
- `locality_domain/autotune.py`: `LocalityDomainConcurrentTunableRunner` / `tune_locality_domain_concurrent` accept an optional `prologue_fn` that runs before the fork on every forward, profiling included.
- `fused_moe_cute_dsl.py`: raw activations reach the split like the full-GPU op (the quant fusion no longer depends on the recorded per-token decision; `_mxfp8_full_gpu_path_selected` is removed) and the split path passes `zero_output` under the same dense-case rule instead of launching the separate memset.

Per split call: routing, one parent reset, two shard GEMMs (4 launches) instead of routing, quantize, memset, two resets, two shard GEMMs (6 launches + event pair). Locality domains stay **off by default**.

## Verification (Rubin SM107, wheel built from feat/rl_rc, python overlaid)

- `test_cute_dsl_moe.py -k locality_domain_op_matches_full_gpu`: 2 passed. Adds a split call with raw BF16 input and a dirty (3.0-filled) output under `zero_output`; it matches the E4M3 split and the full-GPU op within the split tolerance. (The two shards scatter-add concurrently with BF16 atomics, so runs are not bitwise identical to each other; the test compares within tolerance.)
- CPU: composite ownership / fake signature / concurrent tunable runner / input-quant and admission rules: 18 passed. `test_fc12_input_quant.py`: 39 passed. `test_locality_domain_planner.py`: 55 passed, 7 skipped. `test_moe_backend.py -k cutedsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12`: 3 passed.

## Performance (same wheel, module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz)

CUDA-graph replays, 4 module copies rotated so weights are cold in L2, Qwen3.5-397B geometry (512 experts, top-k 10, hidden 4096, intermediate 1024), power-law routing (alpha 0.8), worst rank per token count. Microseconds; "off" = locality domains disabled (unchanged by this PR), "on" = enabled with this PR.

| layout | tokens/rank | off | on (before) | on (this PR) | vs off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEP8 (64 local experts) | 4 | 17.99 | 19.60 | 17.65 | -2% |
| | 8 | 22.21 | 22.32 | 20.65 | -7% |
| | 16 | 28.72 | 27.62 | 25.72 | -10% |
| | 32 | 34.19 | 36.19 | 28.73 | -16% |
| | 64 | 45.85 | 46.31 | 37.74 | -18% |
| | 128 | 58.20 | 60.81 | 49.73 | -15% |
| | 256 | 66.44 | 70.09 | 55.36 | -17% |
| DEP4 (128 local experts) | 8 | 52.12 | 53.33 | 43.51 | -17% |
| | 16 | 74.54 | 73.05 | 60.32 | -19% |
| | 32 | 100.60 | 98.24 | 81.13 | -19% |
| DEP16 (32 local experts) | 4 | 25.95 | 30.50 | 24.35 | -6% |
| | 16 | 37.76 | 41.54 | 34.74 | -8% |
| | 32 | 43.01 | 46.32 | 40.16 | -7% |

1-2 tokens are within noise (the selector keeps the full-GPU op there). nsys at 16 tokens, forced split: routing 0-3.2 us, parent reset 2.9-4.3 us (overlapping routing under PDL), shard GEMMs 3.8-23.9 / 4.3-25.1 us on the two partition streams; 4 kernels per call. The shard GEMMs also got faster (22.7 -> 20.1 us) without the quantize launch competing for the GPU.

## Commit 2: static planner decision (as for NVFP4 / BF16), shards are the only copy

The MXFP8 split was a per-shape runtime choice: the autotuner profiled the full-GPU op and the split side by side, a per-token decision picked one (inside a 2048-row / 4096-route admission rule), and to keep that option open the module kept **both** the full expert weights and the shards resident, doubling the MoE weight memory whenever the flag was on. This commit follows the NVFP4 and BF16 paths: with `enable_locality_domains` the planner decides once, every shape of the layer runs the split (its tile / weight-streaming tactics stay autotuned), and `post_load_weights` releases the full parameters after sharding. The selector, its decision cache and the admission rule are removed. A refit after the release (RLHF) re-creates the full parameters transiently in `load_weights`; `post_load_weights` re-shards and releases them again.

**Bug fix (latent in #19469 and in the tekit MR):** the shard block scales were unswizzled and re-swizzled with the module's NVFP4 scale-vector size (16) instead of the MXFP8 block size (32), so the split computed with wrong scales whenever it ran. The op-level test did not catch it because it slices shards with its own helper; the flag is off by default, so the merged default path is unaffected.

**New test** `test_moe_module_mxfp8_locality_domain_static_split_rubin` (2 passed on Rubin): shards an MXFP8 layer, checks the full parameters and quant scales are released, checks the shards concatenate to exactly the base weights, compares the split against the full-GPU module at 16 and 4096 rows (0.5% RMS relative, cosine 0.99999: the shards' extra BF16 rounding of the partial FC2 sums at ~1e5 output magnitude; the MXFP8 quantization itself sits at 2.7% RMS from exact math) and repeats after a refit reload. All other sections re-pass (split op 2, CPU rules 18, kernel 39, planner 55, backend A/B 3).

**Performance, same node and wheel** (Rubin, module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, cold weights, HBM 4752 MHz, Qwen3.5-397B geometry, power-law routing, worst rank, us):

| layout | tokens/rank | off | on (static split) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEP8 | 1 / 2 | 14.80 / 15.18 | 14.30 / 14.70 | -3% |
| | 4 / 8 | 17.53 / 20.51 | 20.11 / 21.89 | +15% / +7% |
| | 16 / 32 | 25.12 / 30.89 | 24.88 / 29.03 | -1% / -6% |
| | 64 / 128 / 256 | 42.24 / 58.61 / 66.95 | 37.50 / 49.58 / 55.43 | -11% / -15% / -17% |
| DEP4 | 1 / 2 / 4 | 20.52 / 26.69 / 35.42 | 22.55 / 25.29 / 33.56 | +10% / -5% / -5% |
| | 8 / 16 / 32 | 53.30 / 75.31 / 101.00 | 43.19 / 61.18 / 81.17 | -19% / -19% / -20% |
| DEP16 | 1 / 2 / 4 | 17.92 / 23.37 / 25.78 | 18.45 / 23.03 / 23.77 | +3% / -1% / -8% |
| | 8 / 16 / 32 | 32.03 / 38.02 / 42.74 | 30.29 / 34.63 / 40.46 | -5% / -9% / -5% |

Without a runtime choice the split costs 7-15% at TEP8 4-8 tokens and 3-10% at 1 token/rank on DEP; it saves 5-20% everywhere else and the weight memory no longer doubles. Prefill-sized rows also run the split (about 20% slower than the full-GPU op at 16K rows/rank in isolated measurements), so enable the flag on decode (generation) engines, as for the NVFP4/BF16 splits.

## TEP8 sweep, 1 to 16384 tokens, all versions on one node

This is the authoritative TEP8 table: all arms ran back to back on one node. The earlier per-commit tables above combined an "on" arm from one job with an "off" arm from another node, and at 1-8 tokens the node-to-node and autotune variance (about 1-2 us) is as large as the effect, so their small-token rows should not be read as precise; from 16 tokens/rank up the differences dwarf the variance.

Same wheel, same node (Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz), module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, cold weights (4 module copies), Qwen3.5-397B geometry, power-law routing, worst rank, microseconds. "off" is the full-GPU path, identical in every version. "base" is feat/rl_rc at f94eeb3738 with locality on (runtime selector, admission rule up to 2048 rows; its split ran with the wrong shard scales, which affects results but not timing). "c1" is the first commit of this PR (parent reset, selector kept), "c2" the second (static split, shards only).

| tokens | off | base on | | c1 on | | c2 on | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 14.99 | 15.32 | +2% | 14.93 | 0% | 14.25 | -5% |
| 2 | 15.56 | 16.05 | +3% | 15.70 | +1% | 14.84 | -5% |
| 4 | 18.03 | 19.39 | +8% | 18.06 | 0% | 20.06 | +11% |
| 8 | 22.26 | 22.05 | -1% | 22.94 | +3% | 22.54 | +1% |
| 16 | 29.99 | 28.04 | -7% | 30.28 | +1% | 26.25 | -13% |
| 32 | 33.74 | 33.56 | -1% | 30.92 | -8% | 31.22 | -8% |
| 64 | 42.50 | 46.67 | +10% | 42.33 | 0% | 42.30 | 0% |
| 128 | 58.63 | 61.55 | +5% | 55.21 | -6% | 55.50 | -5% |
| 256 | 66.37 | 69.49 | +5% | 62.44 | -6% | 62.17 | -6% |
| 512 | 74.12 | 76.74 | +4% | 68.96 | -7% | 68.63 | -7% |
| 1024 | 78.62 | 82.05 | +4% | 73.30 | -7% | 72.93 | -7% |
| 2048 | 88.94 | 93.97 | +6% | 84.66 | -5% | 85.56 | -4% |
| 4096 | 112.16 | 112.02 | 0% | 112.09 | 0% | 111.22 | -1% |
| 8192 | 157.07 | 156.77 | 0% | 158.18 | +1% | 176.58 | +12% |
| 16384 | 228.69 | 228.60 | 0% | 230.09 | +1% | 281.58 | +23% |

- Before this PR the selected split was mostly a loss (4-10% slower from 64 to 2048 tokens) because of its two resets, separate quantize and separate memset; above 2048 the admission rule kept the full-GPU op.
- Commit 1 turns the selected split into a 5-8% gain from 32 through 2048 tokens with no change elsewhere.
- Commit 2 (static, one weight copy) matches or beats commit 1 wherever the split runs (-5% at 1-2 tokens, -13% at 16, -4..-8% at 32-2048) and adds the two costs of having no shape filter: +11% at 4 tokens, and the prefill penalty at 8K-16K rows/rank (+12% / +23%, the inner-channel split's tile-efficiency loss once the kernel is compute-bound). As with the NVFP4/BF16 splits, enable the flag on decode (generation) engines and leave it off on context engines.

## Same-node check of the cached-FC2 tactic removal (commit 3) and node sensitivity

Rubin, one node (a different one from the sweep above), same wheel, TEP8 worst rank, cold weights, us:

| tokens | off | split, cached-FC2 allowed | split, streaming only (commit 3) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 2 | 14.78 / 15.18 | 15.02 / 14.74 | 14.57 / 14.66 |
| 4 / 8 | 17.58 / 19.42 | 20.13 / 21.90 | 20.12 / 22.04 |
| 16 / 32 | 27.55 / 33.74 | 24.95 / 29.05 | 24.97 / 29.05 |
| 64 / 128 / 256 | 42.23 / 58.67 / 67.20 | 37.51 / 49.59 / 55.46 | 37.07 / 49.18 / 55.24 |
| 512 / 1024 / 2048 | 73.69 / 81.68 / 89.05 | 61.32 / 65.87 / 79.21 | 61.04 / 66.05 / 80.74 |
| 4096 / 8192 / 16384 | 116.78 / 155.95 / 226.67 | 105.95 / 186.30 / 281.00 | 106.12 / 186.74 / 281.56 |

The two split variants agree within 1-2% everywhere (3% at 1 token, within the run-to-run spread), so commit 3 is hygiene.

**How large the module-level gain is, honestly.** Across three nodes the module-level split gain at 32-256 tokens measured 4-8% (hecate0036), 9-19% (hecate0090) and 5-9% (hecate0177, rotation 8); the sign is consistent, the size is node-dependent, and 5-10% is the fair headline. An op-level measurement of the same two ops (E4M3 input supplied, op incl. its own reset, best of both routing tiles, rotation 4 or 8) shows the split only 0-2% ahead of the full-GPU op at 64-256 tokens and 7-15% behind at 4-32. The difference is which rank is called "worst": the module benchmark takes the rank with the most local routes (e.g. 59 routes over 23 experts at 32 tokens), the op-level one the slowest rank by time (43 routes over 27 experts); more rows per expert tile is where halving the inner channels helps a CTA, so the split's advantage is largest on the route-heaviest rank, which is also the rank that bounds the MoE step. Two observations from the traces at 1-16 tokens: (a) at 1-2 tokens (3-5 routes) each half-channel shard kernel is 0.5-0.8 us shorter than the full kernel because a few CTAs are limited by per-CTA weight streaming and each shard streams half the bytes; (b) at 4-8 tokens (9-17 routes) the full kernel is already close to the aggregate HBM limit, so the split cannot cut the bytes and each shard runs 1-1.5 us *longer* than the whole kernel (doubled input/metadata gathers, both shards' atomics on the same output rows, and the slower shard sets the pace), hence +13-15%. From 16 tokens per-CTA FC1 work is large enough for the half-channel split to win and the gain grows with routes. Note the split is more node-sensitive than the full-GPU op: flag-off agrees with the other node within 1-4%, while the split measured 9-19% under flag-off here against 4-8% there at the same token counts.

## Reference: kernel-level TP8 comparison (not part of this PR's change)

One GPU (Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz), TP8 / MoE-TP8 / no EP layout (512 local experts, intermediate 128 per rank), identical power-law routing and weights, E4M3 input outside the timed call, each op incl. its own reset/clear, 8 cold weight copies, us per call:

| tokens | active experts / routes | CuTe kernel at MR 10663 base | ours (feat/rl_rc + this PR) | HMMA (tekit MR 10663) | CUDA-core (fc12-mxfp8-tp8-study, requant mode) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 / 10 | 14.62 | 10.73 | 6.84 | 8.61 |
| 2 | 17 / 20 | 15.02 | 11.82 | 8.04 | 13.89 |
| 4 | 34 / 40 | 17.98 | 14.12 | 10.57 | 19.42 |
| 8 | 64 / 80 | 21.47 | 17.60 | 13.32 | 29.29 |
| 16 | 105 / 160 | 27.04 | 23.79 | 19.58 | 49.16 |
| 32 | 177 / 320 | 35.91 | 32.36 | 35.91 | 84.24 |
| 64 | 281 / 640 | 49.97 | 45.21 | 55.54 | 153.25 |
| 128 | 388 / 1280 | 66.15 | 62.64 | 79.50 | 278.21 |
| 256 | 459 / 2560 | 77.71 | 73.14 | 139.29 | 550.54 |

The HMMA kernel is faster in isolation up to 16 tokens (18-36%) and slower from 32 (11-90%); the CUDA-core kernel wins only at 1 token. In the gen-only rollout the HMMA/TP8 arm was nevertheless 10-18% slower per decode step from 3 concurrent requests up (duplicated per-rank gather/routing work and tail launches under concurrent streams), so the layout decision is not a kernel-time decision.

records.title: [None][perf] MiniMax-M3: native P128 draft KV view for the NVFP4 hybrid cache
records.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The hybrid NVFP4 Eagle draft cache now uses a native FP8/P128 view and device-side block-offset copying. The change removes the P32 sub-page draft path and updates the draft-view accessor and hybrid-layer predicate. The reported B300 result improves batch-32 decode time at 128k context from 38.4 ms to 20.9 ms per step; the FP8-KV reference was 19.9 ms. These are author-reported measurements, not independently verified here.

FP8 and BF16 cache paths are reported as unaffected. The author reports matching token and decode-step counts in a 24-prompt greedy acceptance probe. Multi-GPU SM100, attention-DP, disaggregated-serving, and pipeline-parallel runs remain unvalidated. The supplied evidence does not establish test execution results.

## QA Engineer Review

The supplied change summary identifies updates to `test_minimax_m3_shared_draft_layers.py` and `test_minimax_m3_dense_decode.py`. Coverage includes native P128 table copying, view geometry and validation errors, pool selection, hybrid-layer exclusions, accessor behavior, and unsupported multiple local draft layers. The author reports 153 tests passed with the change and 147 without it across the named M3 tests and `test_msa_backend.py`; these results are not independently verified. The changed tests were not found in the searched CI or manual-QA list files. **Coverage verdict: needs follow-up** for the unvalidated integration configurations.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/minimax_m3/cache_manager.py` — Verify FP8/P128 view pool pointers, block-table copying, and rejection of unsupported page geometry. Confirm block lifecycle remains owned by the shared manager.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/minimax_m3/kernels/msa_scatter.py` — The subpaged FP8 scatter path is removed. Verify no remaining caller requires `fused_write_subpaged_layer_caches`.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/minimax_m3/kernels/trtllm_gen_dense_decode.py` — Hybrid draft layers are excluded from subpage-factor selection. Verify dense decode still selects the correct staged table for other layers.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_minimaxm3.py` — The reported change is a comment update only; no QA behavior change is identified.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py` — Scratch-copy preparation now reads role-specific page-index conversion data and rejects expansion factors other than one. Verify supported scratch-copy paths and the rejection path.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/interface.py` — The draft cache manager lookup uses the renamed view accessor. Verify the speculative metadata path passes the view to the draft attention path.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/utils.py` — Draft cache lookup now requests the view after checking for an explicitly registered manager. Verify both lookup outcomes.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/msa/test_minimax_m3_shared_draft_layers.py` — Tests cover P128 copying, pool mapping, accessor behavior, and unsupported layouts. The test was not found in the searched integration test lists.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/msa/test_minimax_m3_dense_decode.py` — Tests cover hybrid/NVFP4 exclusion from subpage-factor selection and dense decode behavior. The test was not found in the searched integration test lists.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

With an NVFP4 KV cache, MiniMax-M3's shared Eagle3 draft layer uses a physical-P32 sub-page view
(`MiniMaxM3DraftSubpageView`, added with the NVFP4 KV support in #19422). Its `copy_batch_block_offsets` rebuilds the draft
block table in Python on every decode `prepare()`:
- it lists each request's full padded page row (`max_blocks_per_seq`: 8196 for `max_seq_len` 1M),
- numpy-parses the rows,
- expands them 4x into P32 sub-pages on the CPU,
- and copies the result H2D.

That costs about 0.5 ms per request per decode step on the host. At large decode batch, NVFP4 decode becomes host-bound: the
lagging rank's GPU idles, and the other ranks wait in allreduce.

Scope:
- Only MiniMax-M3 with an NVFP4 KV cache uses the removed path. FP8 and BF16 KV caches are unaffected.
- The host cost grows with decode batch size and with `max_seq_len` (the padded row width), not with live context length.

This PR runs the NVFP4-hybrid Eagle layer at native FP8/P128 instead, the same design `feat/m3_with_msa` has used since #18066.
The FP8-KV Eagle draft path on main (#18872) and the NVFP4-hybrid dense target layers already run FP8/P128 through trtllm-gen.
- `_build_cache_config` now only strips the NVFP4 block-scale buffers from the dense and Eagle layers. The Eagle layer no longer gets
  `tokens_per_block_override`; it is plain FP8 at P128 with expansion 1, and the KV budget is unchanged.
- New `MiniMaxM3DraftKVCacheView`:
  - FP8 dtype, P128, with `trtllm_gen_extra_tokens_per_block = {128}`.
  - A single 2-D pool pointer rooted at the draft layer's K page, with `index_scales=[slot_stride]` and `kv_offset=[1]`.
  - The block table is filled by `copy_batch_block_offsets_to_device`, with no per-request Python loop. It deliberately does not go
    through `KVCacheManagerV2.copy_batch_block_offsets`, which would take the per-layer page-table path via `__getattr__`.
  - Guards: exactly one local draft layer, P128, expansion 1, FP8 storage.
- Removed:
  - the P32 sub-page view, `DRAFT_PHYSICAL_TOKENS_PER_BLOCK` and the M3 P32 page-index override;
  - the `_get_attention_op_page_index_params` hook that #19422 added to `KVCacheManagerV2` for that override. That region of the
    shared `kv_cache_manager_v2.py` is back to its pre-#19422 code, so other models see no change;
  - the P32-only buffer helpers and the unused `fused_write_subpaged_layer_caches` / `_fused_subpaged_scatter_kernel`.
- Renamed `get_draft_subpage_view` → `get_draft_kv_cache_view` and `is_fp8_subpaged_layer` → `is_hybrid_draft_layer`.
- The hybrid log line now reads `... 1 shared Eagle layer(s)=FP8/P128, per-layer page tables=<flag>`.

The comment removed here says the shared Eagle layer needs P32 pages for SM100/SM103 kernel compatibility. P32 started as our own
side-branch workaround (#17457) for P128 Eagle kernel issues at the time. #18066 replaced it with native P128 on `feat/m3_with_msa`
for all architectures, and the side branch still runs that way. On SM103 we found no case that still needs P32. If a specific SM100
case led to keeping P32, please point us to it and we will test it.

### Measurements (B300, SM103)

Terms:
- **AgentX**: the SemiAnalysis InferenceX multi-turn agentic replay benchmark, run for 3600 s.
- **C40**: 40 concurrent sessions.
- **P90 interactivity**: 1 / P90 per-request inter-token latency (tok/s/user).
- **tok/s/GPU**: total (input + output) tokens/s per GPU.
- The AgentX and decode-step runs set `TLLM_SPEC_DECODE_FORCE_NUM_ACCEPTED_TOKENS=1.78`: 1.78 accepted draft tokens per step, the
  InferenceX reference AL of 2.78 for max_draft_len=3. So they measure speed only. The acceptance-probe and GSM8K rows run with
  forcing off.
- **Decode step**: the median iteration time with every request at 128k context and block reuse off.

Setup:
- Aggregated serving, TP only (no attention DP), one-model Eagle3 with max_draft_len=3, NVFP4 KV.
- Baseline: #19422 at its pre-merge revision 4d7e78f3e3.
- "+ this PR": the same wheel with this change's Python files copied over it. The changed lines are identical to this branch.
- Other M3 files changed on main after 4d7e78f3e3 (the final #19422 commit, #19113, #19601, #19513, #17974), so the two AgentX points,
  the acceptance probe and GSM8K were rerun on current main; see the second table.
- Reference: `feat/m3_with_msa` 3f30032c48, which has used the FP8/P128 draft view since #18066.

| | #19422 at 4d7e78f3e3 | + this PR | `feat/m3_with_msa` 3f30032c48 |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode step, TP4, 128k ctx, batch 32 / 40 (ms) | 38.4 / 47.8 | **20.9 / 25.0** | 20.5 / 24.6 |
| AgentX TP4 C40, P90 interactivity (per run) | 79.1, 79.9 | **100.6, 100.0** | 98.0, 97.3, 96.8 |
| AgentX TP2 C45, P90 interactivity / tok/s/GPU (per run) | 44.4, 44.8 / 87.6k, 88.1k | **50.7, 50.5 / 93.0k, 93.1k** | 47.7, 48.0 / 89.7k, 89.8k |
| acceptance probe, 24 prompts, batch 1, greedy, forcing off (tokens / decode steps) | 9438 / 2800 | **9438 / 2800** | 9747 / 2825 (different outputs; not comparable) |
| GSM8K accuracy (1319 q, strict match), TP2 C30, forcing off (per run) | 0.9484, 0.9484 | 0.9447, 0.9522 | 0.9477 (1 run) |

**Rerun on current main** (wheel built from 00bdcb6ed, default C++ KV-cache-manager-v2 backend; baseline and this PR interleaved in the
same period):

| | main 00bdcb6ed | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| AgentX TP4 C40, P90 interactivity / tok/s/GPU (per run) | 82.9, 80.4 / 53.7k, 53.4k | **100.4 / 56.3k** (1 valid run) |
| AgentX TP2 C45, P90 interactivity / tok/s/GPU (per run) | 45.3, 46.7 / 88.0k, 88.9k | **50.2, 50.5 / 93.4k, 93.2k** |
| acceptance probe, 24 prompts, batch 1, greedy, forcing off (tokens / decode steps) | 9438 / 2800 | **9438 / 2800** |
| GSM8K accuracy (1319 q, strict match), TP2 C30, forcing off | 0.9545 | 0.9462 |

The second TP4 C40 run with this PR was aborted by the benchmark client during warmup after a client-side
`ClientOSError(104, 'Connection reset by peer')`. The server logged no error, and we have seen the same abort on main without this
change.

Notes:
- Main with FP8 KV on the same 4d7e78f3e3 build (plus the FP8 warmup fix that landed in #19422's final commit) runs 19.9 / 24.2 ms
  at batch 32 / 40.
- The AgentX runs with this PR ran about a day after the baselines, on other nodes.
- In the decode waves this PR is still 0.2-0.7 ms/step behind `feat/m3_with_msa`. From the traces (not isolated), the likely cause
  is that the NVFP4 hybrid cache keeps per-layer page tables on. That adds a per-step page-index conversion, a few tenths of a ms of
  host time plus ~0.6 ms of GPU work at b=32, which the side branch does not run.
- GSM8K: this PR scored 0.9447, 0.9522 and 0.9462 in three runs (mean 0.948); without it, 0.9484, 0.9484 and 0.9545 (mean 0.950).
  Each paired comparison is non-significant (exact McNemar p = 0.13-0.60). Repeat runs of the same build differ by up to 0.75 pt, and
  greedy speculative decoding only emits tokens the target model verifies, so we read this as noise from batch-dependent numerics.
  GSM8K checks the target model only; drafter correctness is covered by the acceptance-probe rows and the CI acceptance floors below.
- In a DEBUG-log run of the acceptance probe, FlashInfer trtllm-gen rejected no draft request. The b=32 decode trace shows the draft
  running `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H128PagedKvCausalPaged...ForGen` (P128) instead of the `...CausalP32...` kernels.
- Only max_draft_len=3 at TP4 C40 and TP2 C45 was re-measured end to end with this change. The lower-concurrency points and
  max_draft_len 5/7 were not.
- **Not validated by us:** SM100 (B200/GB200) end to end, attention DP, disaggregated serving and pipeline parallelism.
  - The updated unit tests run in pre-merge `l0_b200` on SM100. They check the draft block table and pool pointers only; they do not
    launch the draft attention kernel.
  - The SM100 kernel path and attention DP are covered end to end by the 4-GPU pre-merge `l0_dgx_b200` tests listed under Test
    Coverage. This PR's files do not trigger the multi-GPU stages, so those tests need `/bot run --add-multi-gpu-test` and the
    `ci: full pre-merge approved` label.
  - A GB200 end-to-end A/B is planned.
- A mixed-version disaggregated deployment (P32 context server with P128 generation server) would exchange Eagle pages in different
  layouts. We expect that to affect draft acceptance only (target KV is unchanged), but have not tested it.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/msa/test_minimax_m3_shared_draft_layers.py`:
  - P32 assertions are replaced by P128 ones. The GPU test runs the real device copy and compares it against the page-index converter.
  - New: `test_block_table_uses_native_p128_copy`, `test_view_rejects_non_p128_manager`,
    `test_view_rejects_expanded_or_non_fp8_draft_pages` and `test_non_hybrid_cache_has_no_draft_view`.
  - Renamed:
    - `test_hybrid_view_publishes_an_fp8_pool_pointer_from_the_draft_pool` → `test_hybrid_view_uses_the_draft_layers_actual_fp8_pool`
    - `test_draft_subpage_accessor_respects_local_layers` → `test_draft_kv_cache_view_accessor_respects_local_layers`
    - `test_draft_subpage_view_rejects_multiple_local_layers` → `test_draft_kv_cache_view_rejects_multiple_local_layers`
  - Removed: `test_hybrid_view_rejects_non_p32_draft_pages`.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/sparse/msa/test_minimax_m3_dense_decode.py`: added
  `test_uniform_subpages_per_slot_skips_nvfp4_and_hybrid_draft_layers`.
- End to end on SM100, pre-merge `l0_dgx_b200` (4x B200, multi-GPU stage):
  `accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestMiniMaxM3::test_nvfp4_eagle3[tp_size=4-ep_size=4-attention_dp=False-overlap_scheduler=True-fuse_qkv_index_projection=True-eval_mode=inferencex-kv_dtype=nvfp4]`
  and its `attention_dp=True` variant.
  - Both run GSM8K and then a 200-prompt Eagle3 acceptance probe with NVFP4 floors (acceptance rate > 0.78, AL > 3.3).
  - M3 Eagle3 always shares the target KV cache, so both tests go through the new P128 draft view.
- Local run on B300: the two files above plus `test_msa_backend.py` give 153 passed with the change and 147 without it.
  - Setup: the 4d7e78f3e3 wheel with this change's Python files copied over it, and the #19422-revision copy of `test_msa_backend.py`
    (this branch's copy has 4 more tests from #19113).
  - This branch is rebased onto 324a51deff, which includes #19154 (Python KV-cache-manager-v2 backend removed). The measured wheels
    already used the default C++ backend, and the rebase had no conflicts.
  - They were run outside the repo with `pytest --noconftest`; CI on this branch is the reference run.

records.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- `ConfigurableMoE` now exposes `unfinalized_combine_fn`. When external communication is active and `do_finalize=False`, `ExternalCommMoEScheduler` applies this callback to dispatched outputs before communication combine. The scheduler rejects a missing callback and invalid backend output or routing data.
- For NVLink one-sided communication, the scheduler does not request or mark a combine workspace payload when `do_finalize=False`. Verify workspace planning for both finalize settings.
- `FlashinferOpBackend` enables the FP4 contract change only when `TRTLLM_FLASHINFER_FP4_CONTRACT_FIX` is exactly `"1"`. The opt-in path forwards quantization options by keyword and reshapes flattened activation scales to token-major `float8_e4m3fn`. The default behavior remains unchanged.
- No current review findings were supplied, so severity counts are unavailable. Test execution results were not supplied.

## QA Engineer Review

Added `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_scheduler_finalize_before_combine.py` and `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_scale_layout.py`. The tests cover callback invocation and refusal cases, workspace planning, FP4 option forwarding, scale reshaping, and an opt-in CUDA graph path. These are unit tests, not integration tests, so integration test-list status is not applicable. **Coverage verdict: sufficient** for the described code paths. Test execution results were not supplied.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/MOE_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md` — Verify that the documented callback timing and conditions match scheduler behavior.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/configurable_moe.py` — Verify that models can register `unfinalized_combine_fn` and that its unset default preserves existing behavior.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/moe_op_backend.py` — Verify the environment-flag default and opt-in FP4 quantization and scale-layout behavior.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/moe_scheduler.py` — Verify pre-combine finalization, refusal errors, output dtype handling, and one-sided workspace planning for both finalize settings.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_scale_layout.py` — Covers FP4 provider-option forwarding, scale reshaping, and opt-in CUDA graph behavior. This is a unit test, so integration test-list status is not applicable.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_scheduler_finalize_before_combine.py` — Covers callback inputs, refusal cases, dtype conversion, and workspace planning. This is a unit test, so integration test-list status is not applicable.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Two independent pieces, both in the ConfigurableMoE stack.

**1. Scheduler: optional model-owned finalize before the communication
combine.** `do_finalize=False` asks the backend for the unfinalized
`(gemm2_output, expert_weights, expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx)` triple so a
model can apply its own per-`(token, expert)` transform to each expert
output before the top-k sum. Every `Communication.combine` is typed for a
dense per-token tensor, so that triple cannot cross a comm strategy today —
it reaches `.dim()` on a `list` and dies several frames inside the comm
layer. This PR adds `ConfigurableMoE.unfinalized_combine_fn`: a model
registers its per-row finalize there, and `ExternalCommMoEScheduler` runs it
on the dispatched rows just before the combine, so the combine reduces
already-finalized partials. The reordering equals finalizing after the
combine because each term depends on one `(token, expert)` row alone and
non-local slots contribute exact zeros. With no registered finalize, the
`do_finalize=False` + active-comm combination becomes a named
`NotImplementedError` instead of a crash in the comm layer.

The `NVLinkOneSided` workspace plan also stops claiming the combine payload
is in the alltoall workspace when `do_finalize=False`: the backend writes no
payload in that mode, and `combine()` trusts the flag rather than the tensor
argument, so a stale `True` would make `moe_a2a_combine` reduce an unwritten
workspace region and silently return garbage.

No in-tree model registers the hook yet; today every in-tree caller keeps
`do_finalize=False` and comm strategies apart. The mechanism is the generic
scheduler contract for any backend/model that wants finalize to run inside a
communication-overlap region; default behavior is unchanged.

**2. FlashInfer MoE FP4 scale-layout contract fix (opt-in via
`TRTLLM_FLASHINFER_FP4_CONTRACT_FIX=1`).** Two call-contract fixes in
`FlashinferOpBackend`: `fp4_quantize` provider options are passed by keyword
(new provider options may precede `enable_pdl` in the positional signature,
so positional passing can silently bind the wrong argument), and a flattened
linear `hidden_states_scale` is re-viewed token-major as `(num_tokens, -1)`
`float8_e4m3fn` before `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`, whose API requires the
leading dimension to be `num_tokens`. The flag is resolved once at backend
construction (before warmup/capture); default off, zero behavior change.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_scheduler_finalize_before_combine.py`
  — CPU-only, stubbed `moe`/comm objects: happy path (finalize receives the
  backend triple, the post-dispatch routing weights, the dispatched row
  count; output cast down before the combine) plus the four refusals
  (unregistered finalize, backend that ignored `do_finalize`, router weights
  folded into activations, weights/index-map row mismatch) and both sides of
  the one-sided workspace-payload guard.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_scale_layout.py` — fake
  provider: keyword binding of `fp4_quantize` options under flag on/off/unset
  and token-major scale reshaping (0/1/2/16 tokens, routed and unrouted,
  flattened and matrix input, zero-copy asserted via `data_ptr`). One
  GPU-gated case checks the opt-in path against the real provider under CUDA
  graph capture/replay.

[CuTeDSL] Flash Attention v2 for SM120 (Blackwell GeForce)
records.body:
## Summary

Adds CuTe DSL Flash Attention v2 forward pass kernels for SM120 (RTX 5090, GB10 / DGX Spark), addressing the lack of high-performance FA kernels for this architecture.

**Three implementations included:**

### BF16 Kernels (`flash_attention_v2.py`)

1. **CpAsync variant** (`FlashAttentionForwardSm120`): All threads perform both loads and compute using `cp.async` — the Ampere-era approach, tuned for SM120's 101 KB shared memory.

2. **TMA variant** (`FlashAttentionForwardSm120Tma`): Uses TMA (`cp.async.bulk`) with warp specialization — 1 dedicated DMA warp handles TMA loads while N MMA warps compute, enabling load/compute overlap via multi-stage KV pipelining with `PipelineTmaAsync` mbarrier synchronization.

Both use SM80-compatible tensor core instructions (`mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16`) since SM120 lacks tcgen05 MMA. Supports FP16/BF16, causal/non-causal, configurable tile sizes, asymmetric Q/K lengths, online softmax fusion, and register pipelining.

### FP8 Kernel (`fp8_flash_attention.py`)

3. **FP8 optimized variant** (`FP8FlashAttentionSm120Opt`): Uses SM120's native FP8 MMA instruction (`mma.sync.aligned.kind::f8f6f4.m16n8k32`) via inline PTX, with CpAsync double-buffered K/V pipeline, vectorized 4×4 byte transpose via `prmt.b32`, and bank-conflict-free SMEM layout (+16 byte row padding).

FP8 kernel features:
- 4-warp design with register-level O accumulation (no SMEM round-trip for output)
- Inline PTX MMA as workaround for CUTLASS `MmaAtomSM80Type` segfault with FP8 types (#3044)
- CpAsync pipelining: V load overlaps QK GEMM, next K prefetch overlaps transpose + PV GEMM
- Vectorized V transpose using 8-instruction `prmt.b32` 4×4 byte shuffle (no `ldmatrix.b8` on SM120)
- Bank-conflict-free SMEM: +16 bytes/row padding eliminates 8-way bank conflicts for stride-D access

### TMA variant details

- 4D TMA descriptors `(seq, dim, head, batch)` for native multi-batch support
- TMA-compatible `Swizzle(B, 4, 3)` pattern (M=4 required by TMA hardware; the CpAsync version uses `Swizzle(B, 3, 3)` which is not valid for TMA)
- Separate K and V pipelines for independent scheduling
- Configurable `kv_stages` for double-buffering (default 2, falls back to 1 for large head_dim)

## Benchmark Results

### FP8 vs BF16 Performance on DGX Spark (SM121a)

*Updated 2026-06-12: the table below originally predated the `FP8FlashAttentionSm120Tma` variant and an FP8 reference-check fix (`fdd8cf12`) — see [the April analysis](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/pull/3030#issuecomment-4328524695) for full details. Current summary at head (cutlass-dsl 4.5.2, CUDA 13.0, GB10):*

- All 16 benchmark configs pass reference checks, including causal (the earlier causal failures were a test-reference bug — `view` on `(B,S,H,D)` without permute — not a kernel bug)
- FP8 TMA vs FP8 Opt: 1.09–1.14x sum-time, up to ~1.5x at B=4 D=128
- FP8 TMA vs BF16 TMA: 0.81–0.88x sum-time — BF16 remains faster overall at these shapes; the structural cost is the `f8f6f4` B-operand register-layout bridge (~16 shuffles per `ldmatrix` in the PV path). The FP8 path's value is the validated inline-PTX `f8f6f4` route pending #3044, plus the memory-side win.

### BF16 TMA vs CpAsync Performance on DGX Spark (SM121a)

TMA kernel: `FlashAttentionForwardSm120Tma` (warp-specialized, 3 MMA + 1 DMA warp, `PipelineTmaAsync`)
CpAsync kernel: `FlashAttentionForwardSm120` (all threads load+compute, `cp.async`)
Both: M=128, N=64, 16 heads, 20 warmup iters, 100 timed iters

| Batch | SeqLen | HDim | Causal | CpAsync (μs) | TMA (μs) | CpAsync TFLOPS | TMA TFLOPS | Speedup |
|:-----:|:------:|:----:|:------:|-------------:|---------:|---------------:|-----------:|:-------:|
| 1 | 512 | 64 | no | 20.5 | 24.6 | 52.48 | 43.67 | 0.83x |
| 1 | 512 | 64 | yes | 22.7 | 32.8 | 23.60 | 16.39 | 0.69x |
| 1 | 512 | 128 | no | 41.0 | 41.0 | 52.40 | 52.38 | 1.00x |
| 1 | 512 | 128 | yes | 32.8 | 34.8 | 32.77 | 30.85 | 0.94x |
| 1 | 1024 | 64 | no | 82.2 | 65.5 | 52.26 | 65.55 | **1.25x** |
| 1 | 1024 | 64 | yes | 45.1 | 51.3 | 47.66 | 41.85 | 0.88x |
| 1 | 1024 | 128 | no | 112.4 | 110.8 | 76.45 | 77.55 | 1.01x |
| 1 | 1024 | 128 | yes | 85.4 | 86.1 | 50.32 | 49.90 | 0.99x |
| 1 | 2048 | 64 | no | 217.8 | 281.5 | 78.86 | 61.03 | 0.77x |
| 1 | 2048 | 64 | yes | 155.2 | 157.5 | 55.33 | 54.52 | 0.99x |
| 1 | 2048 | 128 | no | 519.7 | 461.3 | 66.11 | 74.49 | **1.13x** |
| 1 | 2048 | 128 | yes | 317.6 | 285.9 | 54.09 | 60.10 | **1.11x** |
| 4 | 512 | 64 | no | 55.3 | 88.9 | 77.72 | 48.30 | 0.62x |
| 4 | 512 | 128 | no | 175.7 | 179.3 | 48.88 | 47.91 | 0.98x |
| 4 | 1024 | 64 | no | 226.9 | 318.2 | 75.72 | 53.98 | 0.71x |

Geometric mean speedup: **0.95x** · Min: 0.62x · Max: 1.25x

> **Note:** These initial results contained JIT compilation artifacts (some configs inflated/deflated by first-compilation overhead) and a causal masking bug — see updated results below.

**Key findings:**
- **D=128, medium-to-large sequences**: TMA wins 6-13% (S≥2048 causal, B=4 S≥1024) — warp specialization amortizes DMA warp overhead
- **D=64**: TMA consistently loses (0.62x-0.88x) — tiles too small to amortize the dedicated DMA warp
- **Short sequences (S=512)**: Roughly neutral for D=128, overhead-dominated for D=64
- **kv_stages=1** (required by SMEM budget for D=128): Limits TMA pipelining benefit — no double-buffering of KV tiles
- TMA's primary advantage is architectural: it demonstrates `cp.async.bulk` + warp specialization on SM120, a pattern that scales better with larger tile sizes and multi-stage pipelining

### BF16 TMA vs CpAsync — Updated (post causal masking fix)

The initial results above had two issues:

1. **JIT compilation artifacts**: The CuTe DSL JIT-compiles kernels on first invocation, which inflated/deflated some configs (e.g. the 1.25x outlier at B=1 S=1024 D=64 was a JIT artifact). The updated benchmark pre-warms all kernel variants before timing.

2. **Causal masking bug** (fixed in `106e24b`): The TMA variant applied expensive per-element causal masking to *all* KV tiles instead of only the `ceil_div(m_block, n_block)` tiles near the diagonal. The CpAsync variant correctly used a two-loop structure (masked loop + fast loop). This caused up to 40% regression on causal configs (e.g. B=1 S=512 D=64 causal: 0.69x → 1.00x after fix).

Updated results with JIT pre-warming + causal fix:

| Batch | SeqLen | HDim | Causal | CpAsync (μs) | TMA (μs) | CpAsync TFLOPS | TMA TFLOPS | Speedup |
|:-----:|:------:|:----:|:------:|-------------:|---------:|---------------:|-----------:|:-------:|
| 1 | 512 | 64 | no | 20.5 | 24.6 | 52.46 | 43.69 | 0.83x |

| 1 | 2048 | 128 | yes | 269.7 | 281.1 | 63.71 | 61.11 | 0.96x |

| 4 | 512 | 128 | no | 160.9 | 206.6 | 53.39 | 41.58 | 0.78x |

| 4 | 1024 | 128 | no | 556.5 | 504.5 | 61.74 | 68.11 | **1.10x** |
| 4 | 2048 | 64 | no | 818.2 | 1040.6 | 83.99 | 66.04 | 0.79x |
| 4 | 2048 | 128 | no | 1784.1 | 1727.8 | 77.03 | 79.55 | 1.03x |
| 1 | 4096 | 128 | no | 1629.5 | 1579.0 | 84.35 | 87.04 | 1.03x |
| 1 | 4096 | 128 | yes | 923.3 | 928.0 | 74.43 | 74.05 | 0.99x |
| 1 | 8192 | 128 | no | 6420.1 | 7276.4 | 85.63 | 75.55 | 0.88x |
| 1 | 8192 | 128 | yes | 3668.0 | 3825.6 | 74.94 | 71.85 | 0.96x |
| 4 | 4096 | 128 | no | 6848.6 | 6269.1 | 80.27 | 87.69 | **1.09x** |

Geometric mean speedup: **0.93x** · Min: 0.77x · Max: 1.10x

**What changed vs initial results:**
- **Causal regression eliminated**: B=1 S=512 D=64 causal went from 0.69x → **1.00x**, B=1 S=512 D=128 causal from 0.94x → **0.93x** (stable)
- **JIT artifacts removed**: B=1 S=1024 D=64 non-causal went from 1.25x → 0.82x (the "win" was JIT noise); similarly B=4 S=2048 D=64 from 1.12x → 0.79x
- **Range tightened**: Min improved from 0.62x → 0.77x; Max normalized from 1.25x → 1.10x

**Updated key findings:**
- **D=128 compute-heavy configs**: TMA provides real 3-10% wins (B=4 S≥1024, B=1 S=4096) where warp specialization amortizes the dedicated DMA warp cost
- **D=64**: TMA consistently loses 5-23% — the N=64 KV tile is too small to benefit from hardware-managed bulk loads vs thread-cooperative CpAsync
- **Causal configs**: After the fix, causal is roughly neutral to slightly slower (0.93x-1.00x) — the runtime branch adds minor overhead vs CpAsync's compile-time two-loop structure
- **Overall**: CpAsync remains the faster default for most configs on SM120. TMA's value is primarily as a reference implementation demonstrating `cp.async.bulk` + warp specialization patterns in the CuTe DSL

## Test Results

Validated on **NVIDIA GB10 (SM121a / DGX Spark)** hardware at [Second Nature Computing](https://joinsecondnature.com) against PyTorch `scaled_dot_product_attention`:

### BF16 TMA variant (`--use_tma`)

### FP8 kernel

| variant | batch | seqlen_q | seqlen_k | heads | head_dim | causal | result |
|---------|-------|----------|----------|-------|----------|--------|--------|
| POC | 1 | 16 | 32 | 1 | 128 | no | PASS |
